### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. pretibial dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.785)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:2214)

**Proposed mechanism:** COL7A1 (HGNC:2214) —DISRUPTS→ Abnormal collagen fibril formation (HP:0005777); Abnormal collagen fibril formation (HP:0005777) —LEADS_TO→ Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (HP:0007327); Abnormal collagen fibril formation (HP:0005777) —LEADS_TO→ Skin fragility (HP:0007243); Skin fragility (HP:0007243) —LEADS_TO→ Blistering of skin (HP:0000985). Loss-of-function mutations in COL7A1 lead to impaired formation of anchoring fibrils, disrupting the dermal-epidermal junction. This disruption results in generalized skin fragility and blistering, manifesting as dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa and pretibial dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a patient with MONDO:0011398 or pretibial dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (MONDO:0007552) who has a pathogenic variant in a gene other than COL7A1, and where COL7A1 variants are absent or benign. _(variant: Any common variant (AF > 0.01) in COL7A1 found to be pathogenic for either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis in COL7A1 provides a unified target for therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring anchoring fibril function or improving skin barrier integrity in both conditions.

#### 2. epidermolysis bullosa with congenital localized absence of skin and deformity of nails  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.782)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:2214)

**Proposed mechanism:** COL7A1 (HGNC:2214) —DISRUPTS→ Abnormal collagen VII deposition (HP:0030177); Abnormal collagen VII deposition (HP:0030177) —LEADS_TO→ Blistering of the skin (HP:0000970); Abnormal collagen VII deposition (HP:0030177) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital localized absence of skin (HP:0011232); Abnormal collagen VII deposition (HP:0030177) —LEADS_TO→ Deformity of nails (HP:0000957). Mutations in COL7A1 lead to defective type VII collagen, impairing its deposition in the dermal-epidermal junction. This disruption results in weakened adhesion between the epidermis and dermis, manifesting as blistering of the skin (phenotype for MONDO:0011398), and also contributes to congenital localized absence of skin and nail deformities (phenotypes for MONDO:0007557).

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in COL7A1 that do not lead to loss-of-function or that are associated with distinct functional consequences in patients with MONDO:0011398 versus MONDO:0007557. _(variant: Presence of common benign variants in COL7A1 in affected individuals that do not segregate with disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis in COL7A1 provides a common therapeutic target for both dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa and epidermolysis bullosa with congenital localized absence of skin and deformity of nails, potentially enabling gene therapy or protein replacement strategies applicable to both conditions.

Mutations in COL7A1 lead to a dysfunctional basement membrane, resulting in skin blistering.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in COL7A1 that lead to distinct functional consequences (e.g., gain-of-function) in one disease versus the other, or if the diseases were found to be caused by entirely separate genetic loci with no shared downstream pathways. _(variant: Pathogenic variants in COL7A1 with a minor allele frequency > 0.01 in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared COL7A1 defect offers potential for developing gene- or protein-replacement therapies applicable to both conditions.

#### 4. neurodevelopmental disorder with epilepsy, spasticity, and brain atrophy  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.397)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-204005)

**Proposed mechanism:** COL7A1 (HGNC:2342) —LEADS_TO→ Epidermolysis bullosa (HP:0001861); TRAPPC4 (HGNC:28854) —DISRUPTS→ Vesicular transport (GO:0006888); Vesicular transport (GO:0006888) —LEADS_TO→ Epilepsy (HP:0001250); Vesicular transport (GO:0006888) —LEADS_TO→ Brain atrophy (HP:0002079); Vesicular transport (GO:0006888) —LEADS_TO→ Spasticity (HP:0001257). Mutations in COL7A1 cause epidermolysis bullosa. Mutations in TRAPPC4 disrupt vesicular transport, leading to neurodevelopmental disorder with epilepsy, spasticity, and brain atrophy. The shared mechanism is the disruption of vesicular transport, a fundamental cellular process implicated in various cellular functions and organ development.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of TRAPPC4 mutations in individuals with neurodevelopmental disorder with epilepsy, spasticity, and brain atrophy, or identification of distinct molecular pathways for each disease. _(variant: N/A)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of vesicular transport in these distinct rare diseases could reveal novel therapeutic targets for neurodevelopmental disorders and potentially other conditions associated with impaired intracellular trafficking.

#### 5. encephalopathy, progressive, early-onset, with episodic rhabdomyolysis  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.387)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-204005)

**Proposed mechanism:** COL7A1 (HGNC:2207) —LEADS_TO→ Epidermolysis bullosa dystrophica (HP:0001072); TRAPPC2L (HGNC:28821) —DISRUPTS→ Protein transport (GO:0015031); Protein transport (GO:0015031) —LEADS_TO→ Encephalopathy (HP:0001290); Protein transport (GO:0015031) —LEADS_TO→ Episodic rhabdomyolysis (HP:0011870). Haploinsufficiency of COL7A1 leads to Epidermolysis bullosa dystrophica. Haploinsufficiency of TRAPPC2L disrupts protein transport, which in turn leads to encephalopathy and episodic rhabdomyolysis. The shared mechanism is the disruption of essential cellular processes due to haploinsufficiency of genes involved in protein function and cellular transport.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that TRAPPC2L mutations do not impair protein transport or that COL7A1 mutations do not affect extracellular matrix formation and integrity. _(variant: Presence of common loss-of-function variants in TRAPPC2L in the general population at a frequency > 1%.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of protein transport disruption in TRAPPC2L-related encephalopathy and rhabdomyolysis, and its potential overlap with cellular processes affected in COL7A1-related epidermolysis bullosa, could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting protein homeostasis and cellular trafficking.

#### 6. developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 96  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.386)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-204005)

**Proposed mechanism:** COL7A1 (HGNC:2207) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization and collagen fibril organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization and collagen fibril organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (HP:0007375); NSF (HGNC:7911) —DISRUPTS→ Vesicle-mediated transport (GO:0016192); Vesicle-mediated transport (GO:0016192) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (HP:0011331); Extracellular matrix organization and collagen fibril organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Cellular homeostasis and protein trafficking (GO:0007154); Vesicle-mediated transport (GO:0016192) —LEADS_TO→ Cellular homeostasis and protein trafficking (GO:0007154). Loss-of-function mutations in COL7A1 disrupt extracellular matrix organization, leading to dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa. Simultaneously, loss-of-function mutations in NSF disrupt vesicle-mediated transport, contributing to developmental and epileptic encephalopathy. Both disrupted pathways converge on a general impairment of cellular homeostasis and protein trafficking, suggesting a shared underlying cellular vulnerability.

**How to falsify it:** If targeted sequencing of COL7A1 and NSF in patients with MONDO:0011398 and MONDO:0023659, respectively, reveals no loss-of-function variants, or if variants in these genes do not segregate with the phenotype, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: A common pathogenic variant (AF > 1%) in either HGNC:2207 or HGNC:7911 associated with both phenotypes would strongly challenge the hypothesis of distinct disease origins converging on shared downstream pathways.)_

**How to falsify it:** If genetic studies reveal distinct and non-overlapping molecular pathways for COL7A1 and SERPINA1 that do not converge on the extracellular matrix organization or elastin degradation processes, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: The identification of common variants (AF > 0.1%) in gnomAD within the coding regions of COL7A1 or SERPINA1 that are not associated with either disease would weaken the causal link.)_
